set.approach: Park along the forest road below the falls and walk in toward the Flood Falls flow. This line is a separate flow roughly 300 m to the left of Mousetrap.
set.descent_text: Parties rappel the route: the first rappel is off trees beside the climb and the second is off the ice.

review.notes: Location relative to Mousetrap and the two rappel anchor types from the route page; area page for access context.

set.approach: Medusa forms in the drainage on the right as you hike west up the hillside above the highway, so the approach is a long bushwhack down into the creek and then a climb up rambling ice steps to the base. It only forms in some seasons.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from the top.

review.notes: Single route page supports the drainage approach and rappel descent; no second source found.

set.approach: A tourist trail leads straight to the base of the falls, a short walk from the road. Mousetrap follows the main flow of the falls.

review.notes: Trail to base from route page and area getting-there line.

set.approach: Park at the pullout beyond the Enterprise Creek bridge rather than at the bridge itself. Walk back to the south side of the creek, follow the old road for several hundred metres, and when the falls come into view turn uphill and climb the snow-covered talus slope to the base. The talus can slide in poor snow conditions, so carry avalanche gear and check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach from area page; route page confirms the falls are visible and the gully to the top.

set.approach: The wall stands beside the Kootenay forest service road east of Canal Flats. Park on the shoulder and walk a short way to the base; the curtain is hard to miss from the road.
set.descent_text: Bolted anchors on the right side of the route serve as a rappel line, and can double as belays.

review.notes: Route page for rappel anchors and walk-in; area page for road location.

set.approach: Start from Julseth Road, crossing the highway and a pipeline before heading uphill. Some parties use a faint trail on the west side of the bowl's drainage gully to get through the steep forest below the face. Reach the bowl at the foot of the headwall, cross frozen avalanche debris, and work up onto the high knoll beneath the face, then straight up to the rockband. The upper snow can be corniced in late season; check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Walk off along the west ridge, a popular hiking route, then return through the bowl to the road.

review.notes: MP route page and AAJ report agree on forested approach to the bowl and the west ridge descent.

set.approach: From the Grouse Mountain lodge, follow Goat Ridge to Crown Pass, then drop right into Hanes Valley. Follow the talus slope down, cut left onto a second talus slope, and climb it to the base of the couloir. Check the avalanche forecast, as the couloir and the slopes above it release.
set.descent_text: After the couloir and the summit ridge, descend the summer route down to Crown Pass, then climb back up Goat Ridge to the Grouse lodge.

review.notes: MP area getting-there and VOC trip report agree on Crown Pass/Hanes Valley approach; descent from trip report only.

set.approach: Use the Hanes Valley approach out of the Grouse Mountain area: hike the Grouse Grind, follow Goat Ridge, and drop into Hanes Valley until the large north face appears on the right. The line works up the weaker ground toward the right of the face.
set.descent_text: Once the roped climbing is over, unrope and hike uphill to the ridgeline, follow the ridge back along your tracks to the Grouse Mountain lodge, and take the gondola down.

review.notes: Approach agrees across MP, AAJ and VOC; descent from MP route page only.

set.approach: Park at the small lot at the north end of Sunset Drive above Lions Bay and hike the steep road. After gaining several hundred metres of elevation, turn left at the unsigned climbing access road, which narrows to a trail and crosses a talus field. Head up and left to the obvious ramp on the north face. The ramp is steep and funnels snow, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Descend the regular Mount Harvey trail from the summit, which runs southwest to the access road and back to the trailhead; large cornices can sit along the upper part in winter.

review.notes: Approach from area page; descent from summer-route page and VOC report agree on the summit trail.

set.approach: Follow the standard route toward Pump Peak. Where the Elsay Lake trail branches off, drop down it until it reaches a broad talus slope northeast of Pump Peak. Cross the talus to the base of the narrow couloir, then swap skis for ice tools. The couloir lies in avalanche terrain; check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: From the saddle at the top of the couloir, return up to Pump Peak and ski down.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: Reach the Centre Creek logging road and cross the creek, then follow the gully, which may be snow-filled, into the basin above the pocket glacier below the Nesakwatch Spires. Cross the bergschrund and climb the couloir between Rexford and South Nesakwatch Spire. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms the Centre Creek side access.

set.approach: Camp above the Houston Glacier, or near Houston Lake if the Melville Glacier is not dropping ice into it. The first technical ground is a northeast-trending crossing of the Melville Glacier to the foot of the rib.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: The shortest way in follows Butters Creek upstream from where the Duncan Road ends, with a long stretch of brush to Butters Lake. Climbers start from a high camp at the saddle northeast of the peak, from which a snow ridge rises to a subsummit.

review.notes: Area page for access; route page for the camp on the northeast pass.

set.approach: Hike the Berg Lake trail to the Dome, where the Kain Face camp sits; mountain bikes are allowed on the first part of the trail, to the shelter past Kinney Lake. Parties also fly to the Extinguisher and cross the glacier to the same camp at the Dome.
set.descent_text: Once the face softens in the sun it is very hazardous to downclimb, so parties wait until the sun leaves and the face refreezes before going down.

review.notes: Approach from the route page (Berg Lake trail confirmed by the North Face page); descent caution from route page only.

set.approach: From the Berg Lake trailhead, hike the trail past the mountain's west end to Berg Lake. Cross the Robson River upstream of the lake, or go farther up and cross over the Robson Glacier's snout. Step onto the Berg Glacier close to its end and climb a minor icefall to the bowl at the base of the face.
set.descent_text: Either descend the face, or continue over the summit and descend the south side by the Schwartz Ledges to the Forster Hut. The south side has complex route-finding, especially from above.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms the Berg Lake bivy for north-side routes.

set.approach: Most parties hike to the Ralph Forster Hut first. Leave the trail at the creek draining the Great Couloir and climb the steep rib on its south side, dodging right around a rock band. Cairns lead left along ledges above the Black Wall to a rappel anchor, then up the ridge to the hut.
set.descent_text: Be ready to build rappel anchors in icy conditions. With enough snow, the steep upper slopes can be downclimbed to the Schwartz Ledges. Some parties stay above the ice cliff, descend the glacier and make one or two long rappels to reach the ridge above Little Robson. Otherwise reverse the ledge traverse beneath the calving serac, then reverse the ascent route.

review.notes: Single route page; area page confirms hut-based south side.

set.approach: From the Forster Hut, go past the first icefall above, then turn uphill onto the neve of the Roof Glacier. Continue to the rock band and look for the hidden gully that cuts through it, leading to the steep snow slope to the top of the Kain Face.
set.descent_text: The descent retraces the route. Marking the top of the gully with wands on the way up helps find it again; if it is missed, the rock face below can be rappelled directly.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: The cirque is reached by helicopter, snowmobile or skis from the Bush River road. From basecamp, hike up the valley keeping close to the left-hand cliffs. The largest and most obvious of the three tiers is near the head of the cirque. The approach and route are exposed to avalanches; check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: Climb the same steep snow slope and first ice pitch as Mexican Overdrive, then traverse a short way right to the base of Blue Lagoon, the centre one of three parallel flows at the right end of the Lyell Wall. The approach has high avalanche danger; check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: Hike or ski up the approach gully from the basin. Deep Throat is the rightmost of the routes on the small wall directly above the gully. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: The approach is exposed to avalanches throughout; check the avalanche forecast. Ascend the steep slope to the foot of the Lyell Wall, coming out just right of Fossen Falls, then traverse left along the wall, staying high, on a long traverse with bolts for running belays. Rappel into a deep gully, leaving a fixed line for the return, climb steep snow up and left to a bolt, and head back right to the base. A rope grab or ascender helps on the fixed line.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: Climb the steep approach slope to the Lyell Wall. Fossen Falls is slightly left of centre on the wall, close to the top of the slope. The slope is avalanche-prone; check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.descent_text: Rappel the neighbouring Fossen Falls line from the bolted anchor at the top of the route.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: The route hides behind a large rock overlap on the far left of the Lyell Wall and cannot be seen until you are below it. The whole approach has high avalanche danger; check the avalanche forecast. Climb the steep slope to the wall's base, emerging just right of Fossen Falls, then traverse left, staying high, with bolts as running belays. Rappel into a deep gully, leaving a fixed line to climb out, then go up steep snow to a bolt, across to another, and up to the base.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: The route is on the northeast side of the cirque. Steep snow slopes lead to the start, and avalanche danger on the approach is high; check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: The route is on the Popsicle Wall, the first big wall on your left on entering the cirque. It resembles a tuning fork and sits directly above basecamp, a short walk up from the hut, with little avalanche exposure on the approach.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: Hike or ski up the approach gully to the base of Deep Throat, then traverse along the wall to the west (left). Quarantine is the left-hand one of the two middle lines on that small wall. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: The route is on the east wall of the cirque, in the gash that runs up the middle of three similar features. A steep but straightforward snow slope leads to the base of the first pitch; it is avalanche-prone, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: The whole approach has high avalanche danger; check the avalanche forecast. Ascend the steep slope to the foot of the Lyell Wall, coming out just right of Fossen Falls, then traverse left, staying high, with bolts as running belays. Rappel into a deep gully, leaving a fixed line to climb out, go up steep snow past two bolts, and make a final short rappel to the start. A rope grab helps on the fixed line.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: A long, avalanche-prone slope leads up to the base of the Lyell Wall, followed by a short traverse right to the start. Sun Pillar is the third of four obvious ice routes, just right of centre on the wall. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.
